description: distillation tasks with the independent Python program's stdout as expected output

tasks.title: Stairwell Fire Code
tasks.prompt:
A small office building has a stairwell with 9 steps. The fire code requires that a person climbs the stairwell taking either 1 step or 2 steps at a time. However, steps 4 and 7 are currently blocked by stored boxes, so no climb may land on step 4 or step 7.

Count the number of distinct ways a person can climb from step 0 to step 9 without ever landing on a blocked step.

Print exactly two lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
Blocked steps: 4, 7
Ways to reach step 9: N

where N is the integer count.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Blocked steps: 4, 7
Ways to reach step 9: 3
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Beekeeper Hive Boxes
tasks.prompt:
A beekeeper stacks honey supers on a hive. There are 6 supers that must be placed in order (super 1 first, super 6 last). Each super has a weight in kilograms:
Super 1: 12
Super 2: 9
Super 3: 15
Super 4: 7
Super 5: 11
Super 6: 8

The hive can hold at most 40 kilograms. Supers must be placed consecutively starting from super 1; you stop placing supers as soon as adding the next super would exceed 40 kilograms. Find the number of supers placed and their total weight.

Print exactly two lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
Supers placed: N
Total weight: W

where N is the integer count and W is the integer weight.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Supers placed: 3
Total weight: 36
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Parking Garage Levels
tasks.prompt:
A parking garage has levels 0 through 4. You start at level 0 and want to reach level 4. From any level you may go up 1 level or up 2 levels (never down). The number of free spaces on each level is:
Level 0: 5
Level 1: 3
Level 2: 8
Level 3: 2
Level 4: 6

Find the maximum number of free spaces you can pass through (counting only levels you actually land on, including level 0 and level 4) on any valid route from level 0 to level 4.

Print exactly one line in this format (no trailing spaces):
Max free spaces passed: N

where N is the integer total.
tasks.expected_stdout: Max free spaces passed: 24
tasks.category: table-based dynamic programming (counting ways, best totals, reachability) with small fixed inputs

tasks.title: Warehouse Pallet Stacks
tasks.prompt:

Pallet 2: 11
Pallet 3: 17
Pallet 4: 9
Pallet 5: 13
Pallet 6: 16
Pallet 7: 10

A forklift can lift pallets only if the stack it is building is at most 60 centimetres tall. Starting from an empty stack, you add pallets in order and stop before adding any pallet that would make the stack exceed 60 centimetres. Find how many pallets you can stack and the final stack height.

Pallets stacked: N
Stack height: H

Planter 2: T (4 litres) or B (1 litre)

Planter 4: T (5 litres) or B (2 litres)
Planter 5: T (1 litre) or B (4 litres)

Min water: N

tasks.title: Lighthouse Rotation
tasks.prompt:
You are programming the rotation controller for a small coastal lighthouse. The controller cycles through a fixed sequence of lens settings as it sweeps the horizon. The settings are defined as an array of Real values representing the light intensity at each step of one full rotation: 0.4, 1.2, 0.8, 1.6, 0.2, 1.0.

For a full sweep, the controller runs through the sequence starting at index 0, then again starting at index 1, then index 2, and so on, until it has started at every index in the array. When a start index is given, the controller reads values wrapping around to the beginning when it passes the end of the array. For each start index, print the sum of the values read over one full pass through the array.

Print exactly 6 lines, one per start index, in order from start index 0 to start index 5. Each line must be in the format:
START=<n> SUM=<value>
where <n> is the starting index (0 through 5) and <value> is the sum rounded to 2 decimal places, with no trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
START=0 SUM=5.20
START=1 SUM=5.20
START=2 SUM=5.20
START=3 SUM=5.20
START=4 SUM=5.20
START=5 SUM=5.20
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Ferry Deck Markings
tasks.prompt:
A small ferry has a car deck marked with numbered parking bays in a single row, numbered 1 through 10. On a particular crossing, cars occupy the following bays: 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 10.

A "free run" is a maximal contiguous group of unoccupied bays. For example, bays 3 and 4 form one free run, and bay 8 and bay 9 form another free run.

Compute the list of free runs on the deck. Print exactly 3 lines, one per free run, ordered by starting bay ascending. Each line must be in the format:
RUN=<start>-<end> LENGTH=<len>
where <start> and <end> are the first and last bay numbers in the run, and <len> is the number of bays in the run (an integer). No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
RUN=3-4 LENGTH=2
RUN=8-9 LENGTH=2
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Weather Station Gust Log
tasks.prompt:
A weather station records wind gusts during a single hour. The gusts, in order of occurrence, are measured in metres per second and are given as an array of Int values:
  12, 18, 7, 18, 9, 18, 5, 18, 11, 18, 18

A "peak gust" is a gust that is strictly greater than the gust immediately before it and strictly greater than the gust immediately after it. (The first and last gusts in the log are never considered peaks because they lack a neighbour on one side.) If two consecutive gusts are equal and both are greater than their other neighbours, only the first of them counts as a peak.

For each peak gust found, print one line in the format:
PEAK=<value> AT=<index>
where <value> is the gust speed and <index> is its 0-based position in the array. Print lines in order of increasing index. If there are no peaks, print the single line NONE.

No trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:
PEAK=18 AT=1
PEAK=18 AT=3
PEAK=18 AT=5
PEAK=18 AT=7
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Library Shelf Reshelving
tasks.prompt:
A librarian is reshelving a small cart of books onto a shelf. The shelf has 8 slots, numbered 0 through 7. The cart holds books in this order, each identified by a single character code:
  A, B, C, D, E, F

The reshelving rule: the first book goes into slot 0, the second into slot 1, and so on. After a book is placed, the next available slot advances by 2 instead of 1 (so slots are visited 0, 2, 4, 6, 1, 3, 5, 7 in that order, wrapping around to the start of the unvisited slots if the advance passes the end).

Place all 6 books following this rule. Then print the shelf contents. Print exactly 8 lines, one per slot, in order from slot 0 to slot 7. Each line must be in the format:
SLOT=<n> BOOK=<code>
where <n> is the slot number and <code> is the single character of the book placed there, or the character '-' if the slot is empty. No trailing spaces.
tasks.expected_stdout:
SLOT=0 BOOK=A
SLOT=1 BOOK=E
SLOT=2 BOOK=B
SLOT=3 BOOK=F
SLOT=4 BOOK=C
SLOT=5 BOOK=-
SLOT=6 BOOK=D
SLOT=7 BOOK=-

tasks.title: Train Network Shortest Rides
tasks.prompt:
A small train network has 5 stations labelled 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Direct connections between stations are given as an array of Int pairs, each pair being [from, to] with a travel time in minutes:

  [0,2] time 10
  [2,3] time 5
  [1,3] time 8
  [3,4] time 2
  [2,4] time 9

For each station s from 0 to 4, compute the minimum travel time from station 0 to station s considering all direct connections and any chain of connections (times add along a chain). Station 0 to itself is time 0. If a station is unreachable from station 0, report -1.

Print exactly 5 lines, one per destination station, in order from station 0 to station 4. Each line must be in the format:
TO=<n> MIN=<value>
where <n> is the destination station number and <value> is the minimum travel time in minutes as an integer (or -1 if unreachable). No trailing spaces.

TO=0 MIN=0

tasks.title: Ferry Crossing Times
tasks.prompt:
A small ferry company runs crossings between four ports: Oak, Elm, Bay, and Cove. The company has recorded the travel time in minutes for a direct crossing between each pair of ports. Some pairs have no direct crossing, which is recorded as 0.

The travel time matrix is as follows (row = from, column = to), in the order Oak, Elm, Bay, Cove:

Oak:  0, 45, 90, 0
Elm:  45, 0, 0, 70
Bay:  90, 0, 0, 55
Cove: 0, 70, 55, 0

Write a program that computes the total time for a round trip starting and ending at Oak, visiting the other three ports in the order Elm, Bay, Cove, and returning to Oak. For each leg of the journey, if a direct crossing exists, use its time. If no direct crossing exists (matrix value is 0), the crossing must be made by changing ferries at the port that provides the shortest single-leg connection; specifically, find the intermediate port (among the four) that minimizes the sum of the two legs, and use that sum as the leg time.

Output exactly 5 lines in this format:

Leg Oak-Elm: NN minutes
Leg Elm-Bay: NN minutes
Leg Bay-Cove: NN minutes
Leg Cove-Oak: NN minutes
Total round trip: NN minutes

where NN is the integer number of minutes (no decimal places, no leading zeros unless the value is 0).
tasks.expected_stdout:
Leg Oak-Elm: 45 minutes
Leg Elm-Bay: 125 minutes
Leg Bay-Cove: 55 minutes
Leg Cove-Oak: 115 minutes
Total round trip: 340 minutes
tasks.category: matrix operations on small fixed matrices

S4: 7, 2, 5, 0
S5: 3, 6, 4, 9

S3 restock: n1 n2 n3 n4
S4 restock: n1 n2 n3 n4
S5 restock: n1 n2 n3 n4

Row1: 1, 0, 1, 1, 0
Row2: 0, 0, 1, 0, 1
